Rare serious events including seizures and ECG changes1-3 have occurred after venlafaxine overdoses; in some cases, death has ensued.4,5 Symptoms suggestive of serotonin toxicity may also develop.6,7 Venlafaxine may not be as safe in overdose as some other sero- tonergic antidepressants. A review8 of UK data recording the number of deaths due to acute poisoning by a single drug, with or without alcohol, found the number of fatalities per million pre- scriptions (the fatal toxicity index) was higher for venlafaxine than for other serotonergic antidepressants, and was similar to that for some of the less toxic tricyclic antidepressants. 1. Serotonin syndrome. The serotonin syndrome (p.416) is most often due to the additive adverse effects of two or more drugs that enhance serotonin activity at central receptors; rarely, a single serotonergic drug may cause the syndrome. One such case1 was reported to have occurred in a 29-year-old woman who developed symptoms suggestive of serotonin syndrome 3 days after starting low-dose venlafaxine.
